messages:
maya: FYI customer ACME (acct acme-inc) opened a ticket saying their April 14th CSV export is missing ~18k token rows but our dashboard shows the usage.
maya: They attached the raw CSV and a screenshot of the dashboard daily view. attaching summary below.
maya: CSV sample (first 3 rows):
```
customer_id,model,timestamp,tokens
acme-inc,gptx-8k,2025-04-13T23:45:12Z,120
acme-inc,gptx-8k,2025-04-13T23:59:59Z,300
acme-inc,gptx-8k,2025-04-14T00:00:05Z,50
```

maya: Customer is in America/Los_Angeles (PDT). They asked why their CSV shows most rows on Apr 13 while dashboard groups them into Apr 14.
maya: They suspect missing rows for Apr 14 in the export (they compared to dashboard totals and invoice preview).

joel: tagging @priya @carlos — billing impact? could be TZ misalignment in the export pipeline or a backfill that hasn't landed.
joel: If CSV timestamps are in UTC and their tooling buckets by local date, that could explain "missing day" vs dashboard which uses local tz? what tz does dashboard use currently?

priya: dashboard rollups are tenant-localized (we store user's tz on the account and do rollups with that tz). Exports are supposed to emit UTC ISO timestamps. They should still be plottable into local days client-side though.
priya: Quick theory: export service applies a convert-to-local step *before* bucketing, so rows near midnight could be re-assigned incorrectly during sharded export job.

carlos: I pulled the export job logs for that day (agg-worker-3). Relevant lines:
```
[2025-04-14T07:01:12Z] agg-worker-3 START export shard=7 tenant=acme-inc window=2025-04-14T00:00:00Z/2025-04-15T00:00:00Z
[2025-04-14T07:01:13Z] agg-worker-3 processing row id=... ts=2025-04-13T23:45:12Z
[2025-04-14T07:01:14Z] agg-worker-3 normalize_ts -> 2025-04-13T16:45:12-07:00
[2025-04-14T07:01:15Z] agg-worker-3 write csv row bucket_date=2025-04-13
```

carlos: Looks like the write path persisted bucket_date after localizing, so the CSV rows got labeled with local date (2025-04-13) while the dashboard rollup assigned them to 2025-04-14 (rollup does UTC->local at read-time). That's inverted behavior.

maya: Customer used our CSV to reconcile and saw a gap for Apr 14 in their import tool. They want a credit if invoice mismatches. How risky is this for billing?

joel: If invoice aggregations used the dashboard rollups (correct), billing is fine. But the customer's exported CSV for their accounting is inconsistent -> customer
experience issue. We should offer to re-run an export for their account with a consistent timestamp scheme and offer a one-time invoice credit if their accounting work incurred a measurable cost.

priya: Plan: 1) create a corrected export (force UTC timestamps, no bucket_date rewrite) and send it to the customer; 2) trace code path in export service to see why normalization happens there; 3) run a backfill for Apr 13-15 for affected tenants and mark as completed. I'll own code fix/PR.

carlos: Additional check: we should identify other tenants that enabled "export-localized" flag. I see a feature-flag guard in exports v2 that may have been flipped by accident on 2025-04-10.

priya: yep. found flag flip: deploy 2025-04-10 02:12UTC toggled exports.use_local_dates=true for rollout. We'll roll it back and prepare a hotfix to avoid writing bucket_date into CSV.

billing-bot: note: created billing-escalation ticket BE-9921 for acme-inc; tentative credit amount: $0 until manual review.

maya: I'll reply to the customer with the mitigation (corrected CSV + ETA for backfill + timeline for fix). Also offering a temporary credit and asking if they want a re-run of the invoice preview.

joel: good. Priya — can you also include a short note in the incident sheet about the flag flip and rollout plan? We may need to reach out to top-10 exporters.

priya: will do. I'll also add a small unit test to prevent writes that mutate UTC timestamps into local bucket_date in CSV writer.

maya: thanks all. I'll keep thread updated and paste the corrected export link when ready. :thumbsup!
